note: Player levels, XP, skills and robot upgrades. The player carries 10 parts at first (Game.BaseInventory), 20 with Deeper Pockets X. Engine independent; read by Progression.cs. XP is only ever granted once per instance/definition/zone/robot (see anti_exploit). Completing a whole ordinary item definition (every copy stored) is the main source of XP; sorting single parts gives a little. Skills and upgrades have no level requirement (skill revamp, docs/SKILL_REVAMP.md). 'status': active = in game, planned = reserved for later, retired = removed from the shop (old saves are migrated, never charged).

point_budget.comment: Skill revamp 2026-10-30 (docs/SKILL_REVAMP.md). One full playthrough earns points for this share of all buyable steps (player skill levels + robot upgrade ranks; an exclusive group counts once, retired skills not at all). max level = round(fraction * steps) + 1, computed at start. PRELIMINARY: recomputed when the skill set is fixed; not locked.

destination_curve.comment: Levels come only from completed storage destinations (every assigned copy stored or installed; each counts once per game). Level 1 -> 2 needs 1 completion; then the step from level L to L+1 is max(1, round(c * (L-1)^exponent)), with c fitted so the max level is reached at completion_at_max of the world's completable destinations (any preset, any budget). Early points come fast. PRELIMINARY test curve.

xp_curve.comment: Legacy: XP is still counted (telemetry, workshop score) but no longer raises the level.

levels.comment: A new game starts at level 1 with 0 points; every level-up gives exactly one point. No halfway points, no level bonuses. Player skills and robot upgrades share the pool and nothing has a level requirement; every buyable level costs 1 point (exception kept for now: Request Pickup, 3) and the levels of one skill are bought in order. There are far more steps than points on purpose.

half_definition_note: Partial set credit: when half of a definition's copies (sets of 2+) are stored, this share of its completion XP is paid at once; the rest on completion (total unchanged). Gives set-focused play a moderate, not a large, head start (tools/audit/progression_sim.py: Standard L19 at 51-53% of the work broad vs 39-40% set by set).

anti_exploit.comment: Picking up and dropping items never grants XP; sorting grants XP only the first time an instance is stored, so taking an item out of storage and re-storing it gives nothing.

preset_xp_scale.comment: Per-item XP shrinks with world size so level 25 is reached at a similar completion fraction in every preset. Balance target: Massive completes in ~1.8x Standard's time (items x2.44).

skills.name: Tool Belt

skills.name: Parts Organiser
skills.comment: Retired 2026-10-30 (placement rules): the hotbar always shows the inventory order and copies next to each other share a slot for everyone; Sort Inventory does the sorting. Budget prelim-2.

skills.name: Sort Inventory I
skills.description: Usable (number key): sorts the whole inventory by storage area, then part type, same type together, otherwise in the order picked up.

skills.name: Part Sense I
skills.description: Usable (number key): the nearest loose robot parts within range glow for 2 s.

skills.name: Destination Orders
skills.description: R gives a lasting order: the robot keeps to that destination until it is complete, shows its X/Y and says why when it can't go on. Without it, R is a one-load request.

skills.name: Fleet Coordination
skills.description: Robots count parts already on their way to a staging zone, and storers split the staging zones between them instead of crowding one.

skills.name: Request Pickup
skills.description: H: the nearest free robot comes to you and takes the parts you carry to their storage. (Formerly called Automatic Storage Delivery.) Cost and robot requirement unchanged for now.

skills.name: Automatic Storage Delivery I
skills.description: Usable (number key), aimed at a storage place: puts matching parts from your inventory into it, up to the level per use.

skills.name: Part Afterglow
skills.description: A robot part you looked at blinks once after you look away, so it is easier to find again.

skills.name: Part Radar Plans
skills.description: The drawings for the Part Radar: with one of each of its eight parts in the robot parts pool it is built at the workbench.

supermagnet.comment: Matches the held item's exact definition id; only UNSORTED instances lying in the world (state InWorld, not reserved by robots). Works on non-magnetic materials.

robot_upgrades_note: Robot upgrade trees (docs/specs/robots_and_levels.md §6-7). Bought with skill points (1 per rank) once that robot type is operational; model-level, so every Hoverbot shares them. stat + mode: add = base + ranks * effect_per_rank; percent = base * (1 + ranks * effect_per_rank) (negative = faster for times); rank = behaviour level read by the robot's strategy. The result never exceeds the robot's permanent limits in robots.json. cost_per_rank lists the cost of each successive rank.

robot_upgrades.name: Carrying Capacity

robot_upgrades.name: Set Awareness
robot_upgrades.description: Robot intelligence (design v1.0): weighs how close a started destination is to being complete, but only by the copies it can really reach. Without it the robot takes the nearest part.

robot_upgrades.name: Robot Part Retrieval

respec.comment: Skill revamp 2026-10-30: no free respec any time. The final respec rules are an open design question (docs/SKILL_REVAMP.md); until then the menu has no respec. Debug builds: F8 is a free dev respec (debug_mode).

restoration.comment: Visible restoration: each zone's lamps brighten up to +lamp_boost_at_100 as the zone is restored; the lathe runs again (spindle turns, work lamp, hum) once its zone reaches machine_zone_percent.
